title: James C. Mountflorence to the Secretary of State (Marshall/Madison), Paris, 18 March 1801 (NARA RG 59, T1 roll 1)

system.summary: One-part numerical code of some 600 groups: single letters at the head of each section, words in alphabetical order after them.
system.notes: Full stops join letter groups that spell one word (four names); commas separate whole-word groups. U and V share one group.

prior_solution.where: Madison Papers SS 1 p. 27 and Founders Online: 'key not found'; Humphreys (10 Apr 1801) could not decode a Mountflorence message; web search 26 Oct 2026 found nothing

conditions.human_role: Daniel Bourdeau pasted the catalogue task; the model did the break, located the microfilm frame and checked the transcription

solution.what: Founders notes, web search, Tomokiyo's American list: no decipherment of the letter.
39 code groups taken from the Founders Online transcription into ciphertext.txt (measured: 39 tokens, 25 distinct).
Groups joined by full stops spell words letter by letter; comma-separated groups are words.
9-group run ABCDBEAAD = LUNEVILLE (U=V), 5-group run ABCDB = PARMA, then TUSCANY and DUPONT from shared letters; the treaty of Luneville and the Tuscany-for-Louisiana exchange as probable words.
The 15 letter values rise with the alphabet: one-part code. Word groups bracketed between letters: Spain, France, secret, Florida, Mississippi, the, to, at, but, by.
250 read as both C (TUSCANY) and 'by' (given by France); predicted the C should be 251 and the Founders figure a slip or misprint.
NARA T1 roll 1 found digitised (NAID 211302912); letter located at frame 0097 from contact sheets of frames 82-340.
All 39 groups checked against frame 0097: TUSCANY has 251 (Founders prints 250); the other 38 agree. The prediction held.
decode.py check: all 25 values in strict alphabetical order.
Armstrong THE=972 code (targets/armstrong) compared: different code ('the' 972 there, 688 here). Humphreys's State key ruled out by his 10 Apr 1801 letter.
Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 39 tokens, 25 types, en-modern order 4: reading -2.617 per letter; Verdict: too short.

Read share recounted over cipher words only (README Conventions, 16 Nov 2026), holes by words, sure words only. The coded part is 16 words (four names spelled letter by letter, 12 words from their alphabetical slots); the four words marked [?] (but, the, Mississippi, at) are holes: 12 of 16 read (75.0%), under the 95% bar, so the letter is read in part. Counted by hand from decryption.txt and reading.txt: the reading file sets the coded words in the clear text around them without marking either, so v10_relabel.py cannot reproduce the figure (it reports 0.918, not split).

texts.label: Decipherment of the two coded sentences
texts.summary: Mountflorence reports, on Dupont's authority, that Spain has ceded to France not Florida but the Mississippi (Louisiana) with its dependencies, by secret articles at Luneville, in compensation for Tuscany given by France to Parma.

reading_review.note: Two English sentences that build sense throughout and match the 1800-1801 treaties; four word values marked [?] rest on their alphabetical slot.

texts.note: 16 Nov 2026, cipher words only: 12 of 16 cipher words read (75.0%), the four marked [?] as holes (before 1.0, counted over code groups). The two coded sentences stand in the letter among clear words of the same sentences; the reading file sets the coded words in them without marking which are which, so the count was made by hand from decryption.txt (not split).

gaps.detail: each occurs once in a 39-group message in a one-part code of some 600 numbers; only the alphabetical slot and the sense fix them, and no second message in this code has been found
